subsystem.name: UiPlatformAndOptions
subsystem.responsibility: Reconstruction grouping for the ui_platform_and_options scope: driver and commentary asset path building, the UI object lifecycle cluster (base UI object constructors, per-type component inits, a slider-list destructor), widget state-change handling, UI config-entry serialization, layout initialization, circuit-info page population, track-path UI display, driver-collision broadcast from a UI selection, and the force-feedback output packet builder.

summary: The ui_platform_and_options packet spans 26 functions. The dominant cluster is the UI platform: vtable-installed UI object constructors and init helpers (UiObject base on off_59F140, UiObjectInit, UiSlider, per-type UiComponent inits, UiDatabaseObject, CircuitInfoPage, UiObjectWithFloatParam, UiLoadingPercentDisplay), a slider/list destructor (UiSliderList), widget state-change handlers (UiStateChangeHandler), and UI config-entry serialization plus layout initialization. Path-asset builders cover the driver asset file candidates (pws/tv x Fb/Fe/Sb/Se) and the commentary TB/TE path lookup, plus the profile-icon BMP path and the track-path display updater. Adjacent functions cover a driver-collision network broadcast triggered from a UI selection and the force-feedback output packet packing. Ownership is UNKNOWN for every packet function; every class proposed here is DERIVED or GUESS. No clean multi-state machine is evidenced in this packet.

Builds and validates commentary file paths in pws and tv subdirectories: resolves the driver-name string from *this and the season globals (dword_5EC3D8/dword_5EC428 with byte_5EA438 fallback), formats a directory prefix, appends TB/TE tokens and the extension strings, checks each candidate via FilePathExtensionCheck against the this+3/+8/+13/+18 (pws) and this+23/+28/+33/+38 (tv) slots, and dispatches matching slots to the commentary lookups. Returns 0 unconditionally.

Computes and clamps the scroll position of a cursor-based UI component: reads the total cursor item count via MenuCursorCount_bc90 and the scroll range at this+0x114; writes this+0xEC as ((count-1) * step + range/2) / range or 0 when the range is zero, clamping into [0, count-1]; when count-1 is below the range an auxiliary utility at 0x0047BD90 is invoked instead. If the recomputed state differs from the snapshot, dispatches a virtual notification through the vtable entry +44 with argument 1.

UI-control state-change handler gated by the enable byte at this+0xE0: snapshots the state via ShortComputation_7720, normalizes a lookup string (this+0xA0, byte_5EA438 fallback) through StringNormalizeLookup_a460 using a context base 5772 bytes into the object at this+0x40, and on success compares it against a second string (this+0xA8) via sub_588410, dispatching StateDependentVTableDispatch_7760 with the comparison result. If a second snapshot differs, fires the virtual notification at vtable offset +44 with argument 1. Always returns 0. Invoked by InitDispatchWithVTableCheck (0x004879E0) and sub_487D50 (0x00487D50).

Serializes one UI config entry into an output buffer a2: concatenates the value at this+0x14 (16-bit/wide-string source) into a 256-byte stack scratch buffer via AlignedStringConcat, writes the key prefix literal aSS_6, conditionally writes the key name from this+0xC (byte_5EA438 fallback) via aS_8, and terminates the entry with word_5C30B4. Returns constant 0.

Object lifecycle routine that installs the interface/vtable pointer off_5AD06C into the first DWORD of the object, then when parameter a2 bit 0 is set frees the object itself via FreeWrapper_7bcf. Returns this unchanged. Existing analysis names the object an audio filter, but that label is not independently confirmed.

Unconditional UI initialization sequence on a __thiscall object: invokes the virtual method at vtable+28 with argument 0, the virtual method at vtable+32 with argument 1000, then UILayoutDispatchWithDataPrep(640). Returns 0.

Builds a force-feedback output packet at this+0x938: iterates 4 wheel blocks (stride 296 from this+0x108) clamping each wheel type, scaling wheel force/intensity by 7.0 and the force at this+0x1E8 by 15.0, and packing results into a dword at +0x938 and a word at +0x93C; packs steering/vibration bytes from this+0xC0/+0xAC/+0x98 scaled by 7.0/7.0/3.0 into +0x93E. When the FFB enable flag at +0x98C is set, iterates 17 channels from +0x9A8 setting bitmask +0x940, packing two 4-bit intensities into +0x93F, and clamping three force components to +/-511.98001 scaled by 64.0 (saturating to +/-32767) into words +0x944/+0x946/+0x948; otherwise zeroes those fields. Returns this+0x938.
